name: Creamy Chicken Tortellini Alfredo
pitch: You've got the cream and pasta to pull off a genuinely cozy alfredo — and adding your chicken turns it into a full meal without any extra effort.
steps: Boil a big pot of salted water and cook your pasta according to the package. While that's going, slice or shred your chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Drain the pasta, keeping a small cup of the pasta water aside just in case.

Return the pasta to the warm pot over low heat. Add a tablespoon or two of butter if you have it (or just a drizzle of olive oil), then pour in your cream. Stir and let it thicken for a couple of minutes.
Toss in the chicken to warm through. If you have any parmesan or even just a hard cheese in the fridge, grate some in — it makes a big difference. No cheese? It's still good, just a little lighter.
Season generously with salt, black pepper, and a tiny pinch of nutmeg if you have it. Serve right away while it's silky and hot.

name: Creamy Black Pepper Pasta
pitch: This is the Italian answer to 'I have almost nothing' — pasta, cream, and a heavy hand with black pepper make something that feels way more special than it has any right to.
steps: Boil your pasta in well-salted water until just al dente — taste it a minute before the package says it's done. Save a mug of pasta water before you drain it.
In a wide pan over medium-low heat, melt a knob of butter (or use olive oil). Add your drained pasta and toss to coat.
Pour in the cream and stir everything together. Let it bubble gently for 2–3 minutes until it thickens slightly around the pasta.
If you have any hard cheese — parmesan, pecorino, even cheddar in a pinch — stir some in now. Add a splash of pasta water if it gets too thick.
Finish with a truly generous amount of cracked black pepper and a pinch of salt. That pepper is the whole point here — don't be shy.

name: Simple Chicken Noodle Broth Bowl
pitch: If your pasta happens to be a noodle-style, this quick Asian-inspired broth bowl uses your chicken beautifully and comes together in under 20 minutes.
steps: Cook your noodles/pasta in boiling salted water, then drain and set aside.
In the same pot, add about 3 cups of water with a splash of soy sauce, a small splash of vinegar or any cooking wine you have, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer — this is your quick broth.
Slice your chicken and add it to the broth to warm through (or if it's raw, simmer it gently for 6–8 minutes until cooked).
Add the noodles back in and simmer together for another minute or two.
Serve in deep bowls. Top with whatever you have — a drizzle of sesame oil, some sliced green onion, or even just extra black pepper. Simple but satisfying.
